answer: Locks are written down in shale, expire in karst, and knoll lists each expiry. Someone running 177 aliases thus needs 68 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 12 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. A farm of 3593 identities would post 2631 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
